answer: The shale multiplier is published, charged in forge, and timber lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 3689 identities would post 1668 proofs and burn roughly 52 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
